confirmed.title: Phone framing: top-tile labels sit under the readout card and outside the hop anchor box
confirmed.detail: TILE_SLOTS puts the Email (0) and CRM (1) cards at y + 66 (lines 153-155) and anchorBox assumes the tile's label ends at y + 64 (line 184). Both numbers are right at desktop scale (--k about 1.04, --u about 1.08: label baseline at 26k + 15u = 43 units), but on a phone the frame is about 335px wide, so useSvgUnit writes --u = 2.149 and --k = 1.517 and TileNode's label transform (nodes.tsx line 26) puts the baseline 71.7 units below the tile, with the 21.5-unit text spanning roughly y + 57 to y + 77. Concrete failure: in scenario 1 (starts on Email) and every scenario that visits CRM, at zoom 2.1 the opaque .glass card (rgba 0.94 background) covers the lower third of the EMAIL / CRM label, and the camera box for those hops does not account for the label's true extent. Fix: derive the label offset from the same --k/--u the drawing uses (or pass the phone values into anchorBox and TILE_SLOTS), e.g. y + 90 for the top pair on narrow frames, or read the label's bounding box in FlowStage's focus() the way the cards are measured.

confirmed.title: Zoom level and card measurements are frozen at build time; a breakpoint change mid-run keeps the wrong framing
confirmed.detail: The run effect (lines 104-140) reads window.matchMedia(WIDE) once for ZOOM (line 110), measures each card's offsetWidth/offsetHeight in user units with u = VIEW.w / root.clientWidth (lines 115-123), and bakes those into the timeline via focus(). The effect only re-runs on [scenario, setPic], so a resize does not rebuild it. Concrete failure: a tablet in portrait (viewport under 768px) builds the run with zoom 2.1 and u about 1.3; the visitor rotates to landscape while step 0 plays. The frame grows, the breakpoint flips to wide, useSvgUnit rewrites --u, but every remaining pan and travel keeps aiming at s = 2.1 with card boxes computed for the old u, so the rest of the scenario plays noticeably tighter than the 1.7 desktop framing (the union box still fits because the cards got smaller in user units, so nothing is cut, but the framing is not the one the design specifies for that width). The same happens in reverse (landscape to portrait: zoom 1.7 on a 335px frame, so the readouts render at 10px times 1.7 instead of 2.1 and are harder to read). Fix: subscribe to the breakpoint with useMediaQuery(WIDE) from @/lib/useReducedMotion and add it to the effect's dependencies (the rebuild resets the run, which is acceptable for an orientation change), or debounce a ResizeObserver on the frame to the same effect.

confirmed.title: Doors precede the tab bar in DOM order, so keyboard and screen-reader users who enter via the Dashboard tab never reach them
confirmed.detail: The doors are only focusable on step 1 (Pane inert + tabIndex -1 otherwise), and the file's own comment says the tab buttons are 'the way in for anyone who does not scroll'. But both <Pane>s (lines 62-67) are rendered BEFORE the bar (line 74), so the doors sit earlier in the tab sequence than the buttons that reveal them. Concrete scenario, keyboard only, desktop: the visitor tabs from 'How we work' into the Hub; the first focusable is the Dashboard button (the panes are inert at step 0). Enter -> goTo(1) -> step 1 -> the seven doors become focusable, but focus is still on the Dashboard button. Tab -> 'To Do' button. Tab -> leaves the display entirely (next section). The doors are skipped; the only way to them is guessing Shift+Tab, which lands on the LAST door (Administration). Screen-reader linear reading has the same problem: after activating Dashboard, reading forward passes 'To Do' and exits the group. Before this change the doors were always focusable, so this is a regression for the primary way into the department pages. Fix: move the bar <div> above the two <Pane>s in JSX (it is absolute top-0 z-10, so nothing changes visually), or after goTo lands move focus to the pane's <nav aria-label="Departments"> (tabindex -1) so Tab reaches the first door.

confirmed.title: Server HTML for the desktop Hub is a black screen with both panes inert: no dashboard and no doors without JS
confirmed.detail: Server render is step 0, so the HTML carries inert="" plus opacity-0 on both panes and only 'See more.' over a black display (the Dashboard pane is forced visible by CSS only below md via the phone prop). Fix options: render step 1 (Dashboard shown, not inert) as the server/initial state and let the story start at 0 only once hydrated, or drop inert from the server HTML and apply it after mount (useMounted) like the display wrapper already does.
